questions.q: What does the Law of Expansion say about companies advertising a wide range of products?
a: They become weaker as they spread themselves thinner
They reach new customers more quickly
They build stronger loyalty over time
They can charge higher prices for everything
questions.why: Lesson 1 says broad ranges weaken a company, using delis that sell an array of items as the example.

questions.q: How did Subway become an internationally recognized brand?
a: It narrowed its deli offering
It expanded into many new categories
It undercut every rival’s prices
It bought up smaller deli chains
questions.why: Lesson 1 credits Subway with being the first deli business to contract its range into a clear brand.

questions.q: What does the Law of Publicity say a brand needs most when starting out?
a: Attention, best gained by being first in its field
A large advertising budget from day one
A loyal following before it launches
A memorable logo and slogan
questions.why: Lesson 2 calls publicity essential and suggests originality or a first-in-industry position.

questions.q: What should advertising focus on once your brand is established?
a: Defending your position and your product’s value
Attacking competitors’ weaknesses directly
Flooding every channel with repeated ads
Promising more than the product delivers
questions.why: Lesson 2 says the aim is to hold the ground you have won, not to spam or boast.

questions.q: What does the Law of the Word recommend?
a: Tying your brand to one powerful word
Using a long descriptive company name
Changing your slogan every season
Letting customers write the tagline
questions.why: Lesson 3 cites Mercedes with prestige and Honda with well-engineered as models.
